body_html:
Louisiana has enacted 8 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Louisiana

8 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB459: Provides relative to the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigns passed 2026-06-09

    This law requires a clear disclosure on electioneering communications that use artificial intelligence to create, alter, or digitally manipulate the image, likeness, or voice of a candidate or elected official subject to recall so that it falsely appears authentic. It also expands campaign finance definitions and reporting requirements for persons other than candidates and committees who make expenditures for electioneering communications. It provides criminal penalties for violations with intent to injure a candidate's reputation or deceive a voter.

  • SB42: Prohibits using artificial intelligence to create child sexual abuse materials. (8/1/26) passed 2026-06-09

    This law amends Louisiana Revised Statutes 14:81.1(B)(3) and (9) to expand the definition of child sexual abuse materials to include artificial intelligence generated images that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of a child under seventeen, and to expand the definition of produce to include causing images to be digitally generated by artificial intelligence. The text does not add a standalone prohibition or penalty; it changes definitions used in existing law.

  • HR302: Requests the Legislative Youth Advisory Council to discuss artificial intelligence issues that may affect young people in Louisiana passed 2026-06-01

    The resolution urges and requests the Legislative Youth Advisory Council to discuss artificial intelligence issues that may affect young people in Louisiana. It suggests the discussion may include education of students, parents, guardians, teachers, and other youth serving professionals regarding AI. The council may seek input from specified entities and may provide a summary to the Commission on Civic Education and the legislature.

  • SB346: Prohibits the use of deepfake material against students enrolled in K-12. (8/1/26) passed 2026-05-29

    This law prohibits students, faculty members, administrative staff, and other employees at elementary or secondary schools from using deepfake material against a student enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve with the intent to coerce, harass, intimidate, or maliciously disseminate or sell the material. It defines deepfake and excludes certain political, public interest, newsworthy, commentary, criticism, satire, parody, or clearly disclosed material. It directs the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education and the state Department of Education to adopt implementing rules.

  • SB347: Provides for the crime of "unlawful deepfake" to be added to the definition of power-based violence under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act. (gov sig) passed 2026-05-29

    This Act amends the Campus Accountability and Safety Act to include conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14 involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery within the definition of power based violence. It also updates the deadline for institutions to develop and distribute safety information from fall 2022 to fall 2026 and revises the required content and distribution methods for that information.

  • HB639: Requires disclosure of the use of artificial intelligence in telephone campaign communications passed 2026-05-29

    Requires a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of any telephone call or automated call in a telephone campaign communication that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure. It defines relevant terms, provides exemptions for certain service providers and broadcasters, sets civil fines, and assigns enforcement to the Board of Ethics.

  • HR249: Requests the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education to incorporate artificial intelligence into content standards passed 2026-05-27

    The resolution urges and requests the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education to incorporate artificial intelligence into content standards. It states that AI is transforming the economy and that responsible integration into K-12 education is essential for workforce readiness and competitiveness. It also emphasizes that AI exploration in schools must be safe, private, and ethical.

  • SB110: Prohibits using a child's image to train artificial intelligence to produce child sexual abuse materials. (8/1/26) passed 2026-05-14

    This law makes it a violation to use an image of a child under seventeen years old at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials. It also states that the child depicted does not have to be a natural person for an offense to occur. It provides factors for the trier of fact to determine age or apparent age in prosecutions.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Louisiana. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
